newsitem.title: ITALY: IRI says buyer of its Seat must bid for minorities.
newsitem.headline: IRI says buyer of its Seat must bid for minorities.

text.p: The eventual buyer of a majority stake in Stet 's publishing division Seat will subsequently have to launch a public buy offer (OPA) for minority share holdings, state holding company IRI said.
IRI controls telecom group Stet and is organising the sale of the firm's holding of 61.27 percent of Seat's ordinary shares and 0.93 percent of its saving shares.
Last week it said it had received 26 suitable offers for Seat from both Italian and foreign companies, which it was now studying.

In a statement on Thursday, IRI said the new owner of Seat will have to offer to buy the remaining 38.73 percent of ordinary stock currently held by minority shareholders, as well as 99.07 percent of Seat's savings shares.
The offer must be made at the same price as that paid for the Stet holding.
Analysts believe Seat could be worth more than $2.0 billion.
Newspapers have reported that U.S. telephone company GTE, British Telephone and France Telecom are all interested in Seat, which publishes telephone directories.
